h1:
Snorkeling Koh Lipe
Hin Ngam · Jabang · Koh Yang
intro: Koh Lipe is known for water so clear you can spot coral right from the boat. A snorkeling trip on a longtail hops between several stops in a single day, from the Jabang Channel with its purple-red soft coral to Hin Ngam beach covered in smooth round stones. Here's the program, the prices and what to know before you climb aboard.

blocks.html: What makes Koh Lipe special is the clear sea and coral sitting shallow enough to see without diving deep. A longtail snorkeling trip is something almost everyone who comes to Koh Lipe ends up trying. The boat loops between several snorkeling spots over a half day or full day, and each one has its own draw — some stand out for the coral, some for the schools of fish, and some for a pretty beach where you can hop off and walk around.

Koh Lipe sits inside Tarutao National Park in Satun province, so most snorkeling spots are around Koh Adang, Koh Rawi and the nearby rock pinnacles. The water is shallow, there are plenty of fish, and the reefs are in fairly good shape compared with many places in Thailand.

blocks.text: Inner zone vs outer zone — what's the difference

blocks.html: Koh Lipe snorkeling trips split into two main zones. Most tours let you pick which one to do, or combine both on a full-day trip.

items: Inner zone — close to Koh Lipe, so the boat ride is short and the swell is gentler. Good for beginners and families with kids. The main spots are the Jabang Channel, Hin Ngam, Koh Yang, and the beaches of Koh Rawi and Koh Adang.

Outer zone — the boat runs further out to spots like Koh Hin Son, Koh Dong, Koh Rok Loy and Koh Pung. The swell is stronger but the snorkeling spots are quieter, with more varied coral and fish. Better for confident swimmers who want to dodge the crowds.
Combined / 8 islands trip — covers the highlights of both zones in one day and takes most of the day. Good if you only have one day and want to fit in as much as possible.

blocks.title: How to choose a zone
blocks.html: If it's your first time or you're bringing kids, start with the inner zone — the swell is gentler and the snorkeling spots are shallow and easy. If you're staying several days, add the outer zone on a later day.

items.name: Jabang Channel
items.blurb: The most talked-about snorkeling spot on Koh Lipe. It's a channel between small islets, with purple-red soft coral clinging to the rock walls. When the water is clear and the sun is out the colors really pop, and plenty of fish pass through. There's no beach here — you slip into the water from the boat and swim along behind the guide.

items.name: Koh Hin Ngam
items.blurb: A beach paved with smooth, dark, round stones that turn glossy when the water washes over them. It's a photo and rest stop where you hop off to walk around. Local legend says the spirit of Tarutao curses anyone who takes a stone home — believe it or not, park rules forbid taking stones anyway.
items.meta: Smooth-stone beach · rest and walk stop

items.name: Koh Yang
items.blurb: A small island with clear water, shallow staghorn coral and schools of small fish moving together. It's relaxed snorkeling because the water is calm and shallow, and you can see the white sandy bottom clearly. A lot of people love this spot because the fish come right up close.

items.activity: Meet on the beach, pick your gear, put on a life jacket and board the longtail
items.note: Mask and snorkel are usually included in the tour — try them on and check the fit before you set off

items.activity: First stop, the Jabang Channel, to see the purple-red soft coral
items.note: No beach here — get in from the boat and swim behind the guide, and be careful not to step on the coral

items.activity: Koh Yang, snorkeling over staghorn coral and schools of fish
items.note: Shallow and clear, good for beginners and great for underwater photos

items.activity: Hop off at Hin Ngam beach to walk around and photograph the round stones
items.note: Don't take stones home — it's both a park rule and a local legend

items.activity: Stop at a white-sand beach on Koh Rawi or Koh Adang to relax before heading back to Koh Lipe
items.note: The half-day trip wraps up around early afternoon, leaving the rest of the day to keep exploring the island

blocks.html: The half-day trip takes about 3–4 hours, good if you're short on time or want to keep the afternoon free for relaxing on the beach.

blocks.title: Hit the highlights of both zones in one day

items.activity: Leave from the beach, starting with the inner-zone spots
items.note: Do Jabang and Koh Yang in the morning while the water is still calm and clear

items.activity: Hop off at Hin Ngam beach to walk around and take photos
items.note: The mid-morning light is good for shooting the stone beach

items.note: Most full-day trips include a boxed lunch or a simple buffet

items.note: These spots are quieter, and you'll see more colorful fish

blocks.html: The prices below are a general range from operators on the island. The real price depends on the season, the number of people and what's included, so check with the shop again before booking.

items: Group trip, inner zone — around 650–750 THB per person (gear and life jacket included, with lunch usually included on the longer trips)
Group trip, outer zone — around 750–850 THB per person
Private longtail charter, inner zone — around 1,900–2,500 THB per boat (1–7 people), depending on the group size
Private longtail charter, both zones combined — around 2,700–3,500 THB per boat
Charters usually add food, gear and drinking water — about 250 THB per person extra

blocks.title: Tarutao National Park fee (paid separately)
blocks.html: The snorkeling spots are inside the national park, so there's an entry fee on top. It's 40 THB for Thai adults and 20 THB for children, 200 THB for foreign adults and 100 THB for children. Most tours don't include this in the price, so set aside some cash separately.

blocks.text: When to go, and a word on safety

blocks.html: Koh Lipe opens by season — you can't visit year-round. During the monsoon, roughly May to October, the sea is rough with big waves, many boat operators stop running, and a lot of accommodation and shops close. At times the ferries to and from the mainland are cancelled because of the swell. The best window is November to April, when the sea is calm, the water is clear and you can see the coral well.

items: Check the weather forecast and wave conditions before every boat trip — if the swell is unusually strong, don't push it
Wear a life jacket the whole time you're in the water, even if you can swim, because the current is strong at some spots
Stay close to the guide and the group, and don't swim off far on your own
Use reef-safe sunscreen — some sunscreens damage the coral
If you get seasick easily, bring medication, especially on outer-zone trips where the boat runs further out

blocks.title: Help protect the Koh Lipe sea
blocks.html: Don't touch, step on or take coral and shells, don't take stones from Hin Ngam beach, and carry every piece of trash back to dispose of on the island. Water this clear only stays that way if everyone pitches in.

items.name: Book ahead or book on the island
items.blurb: It's busy in high season, so you can book ahead at your accommodation or at the tour shops on Walking Street. Prices on the island tend to be similar, so it's fine to compare two or three shops first.

items.name: What to bring
items.blurb: Wear your swimwear from your accommodation, and bring a towel, reef-safe sunscreen, sunglasses, cash for the park fee and a waterproof pouch for your phone.

items.name: Island prices run higher than the mainland
items.blurb: Food and supplies on Koh Lipe cost noticeably more than on the mainland because everything has to be shipped over, so budget for it. You can bring some drinking water and snacks over from the mainland.

faq.q: Should I pick the inner or outer zone for snorkeling Koh Lipe?
faq.a: If it's your first time or you're bringing kids, go with the inner zone — it's a short ride, the swell is gentle, and the snorkeling spots are shallow and clear, like Jabang, Hin Ngam and Koh Yang. The outer zone is better for confident swimmers who want to avoid the crowds, but the swell is stronger and the boat runs further out.

faq.q: How much does snorkeling Koh Lipe cost?
faq.a: A group inner-zone trip is around 650–750 THB per person and the outer zone is around 750–850 THB per person. A private longtail charter starts around 1,900 THB per boat. None of that includes the Tarutao National Park fee — 40 THB for Thais and 200 THB for foreigners.

faq.q: Can I snorkel Koh Lipe if I can't swim?
faq.a: Yes. Every trip provides life jackets and a guide keeps an eye on you, but tell the guide upfront that you can't swim, pick the shallow spots, and stay close to the group the whole time. Don't swim off far on your own.

faq.q: What's the best time of year to snorkel Koh Lipe?
faq.a: November to April, when the sea is calm, the water is clear and you can see the coral well. During the monsoon from May to October the sea is rough, many operators stop running and a lot of accommodation closes, so check before you plan.

faq.q: What should I bring for a snorkeling trip?
faq.a: Wear your swimwear from your accommodation, and pack a towel, reef-safe sunscreen, sunglasses, cash for the park fee and a waterproof pouch for your phone. Snorkel gear and life jackets are usually provided by the tour.
